### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ef194d79777b88379a43b9954177810995e2d3ec` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1c724958721c3dc7c3e594865aabd35ded9e0d58` — the merge of head `cc857c5dc0d292ee3d1bac38f8b9144c20c0fd2d` into base `ef194d79777b88379a43b9954177810995e2d3ec`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1c724958721c3dc7c3e594865aabd35ded9e0d58 && git checkout 1c724958721c3dc7c3e594865aabd35ded9e0d58
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ef194d79777b88379a43b9954177810995e2d3ec cc857c5dc0d292ee3d1bac38f8b9144c20c0fd2d && git checkout -B drift-repro ef194d79777b88379a43b9954177810995e2d3ec && git merge --no-ff cc857c5dc0d292ee3d1bac38f8b9144c20c0fd2d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ef194d79777b88379a43b9954177810995e2d3ec
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## ACCEPT · PR #31870 · #31834 · 2026-11-09T08:51Z

Head-sha: `cc857c5dc0d292ee3d1bac38f8b9144c20c0fd2d`

- **Seat review (TIER_DEFAULT; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; no contract review is owed, because no published schema, export or governed path moves):**
  - **Ruling (c), widened** (seat ruling to the card thread, recorded in the dev report 6735614390). A catalog list request on the public-snapshot path is answered from the snapshot only when every query key it carries is one the snapshot evaluates (`SNAPSHOT_EVALUATED_LIST_PARAMS`: `q`, `limit`, `offset`, `maturity` and the three `CATALOG_FACETS`). Any other key makes `tryPublicMarketplaceFetch` return `null` before the snapshot fetch, so the request takes the existing cloud path with its query string verbatim. `languages` is not special-cased, so the next facet the cloud adds can't be silently ignored here either. Right.
  - **The set is derived, not restated.** The facet keys come from `CATALOG_FACETS`, the same table `readCatalogListQuery` reads, so adding a facet to the reader adds it to the set. The guard is scoped to `packages.json`, so other snapshot-backed paths are unchanged.
  - **Guardrail measured:** the console's `listMarketplacePackages` is the only catalog-list caller, and it sends only evaluated keys. So the cold-start bypass stays on for every console request without `languages`.
  - **Counts:** the cloud answers them on the forwarding path, and no response shape is assumed here. No follow-up is owed.
  - **Failure mode:** with the cloud unreachable, a `languages` read answers the existing `502 MARKETPLACE_PROXY_FAILED`, never a silent 200. The changeset says so.
- **Dev's measured conditions (report 6735614390):** 5 cases in the shared proxy harness: `languages` bare; `languages` with a page window, where the cloud body's extra facets key survives; a made-up key; CONTROL with evaluated keys only, which stays on the snapshot; and CONTROL with the forwarding path unchanged. Base source gives 3 failed / 18 passed; the head gives 21/21. The ablation (delete the early return) turns the same 3 red, and was restored to blob == HEAD. The package's 1127 tests and its typecheck pass, and eslint exits 0. 67/67 derived gates pass with 0 NOT-MEASURED.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and patch for cloud-connection, per ruling A on #25105. Claim 6735015617 covers every file in the diff (3 files, +99/-1; `marketplace-public-url.ts` is untouched and its comment still holds).
- **Gates on this head:** 35 success, 15 skipped, 0 failed or pending on `cc857c5d`; NOT governed (0 of 3 paths); K = 13; mergeable_state clean.
- **Landing:** `pr_ready` and `automerge_enable` happen in this stroke. The card closes on merge (`Fixes #31834`).
